definition_en: to arrange for a company to pay for loss or damage, or to make something certain
core_image: 把一件贵重东西交到窗口，换回一张写着「我替你担着」的凭证
scene: 柜员把贵重的相机仔细包好，又在单据上盖章。 Please insure the parcel before you send it abroad.
sceneCN: 这里 insure 是「给……投保」（第 1 个义项：为物品买保险），句意为寄往国外前请先给包裹投保。画面里的物件：相机、单据、印章。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ance 构成，义为「保险」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「保险公司」
由过去分词转作名词，义为「被保险人」
由本词加 -able 构成，义为「可承保的」

senses.title: Buy cover for something
senses.definition: to pay a company regularly so that it will pay you if the thing named is lost or damaged
senses.definitionCN: 定期付钱给公司，以便所指定的东西丢失或损坏时由它赔付
senses.example: They insured the piano before the movers arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 搬迁工来之前他们给钢琴投了保。
senses.why: Old French enseurer meant to make sure; the commercial sense grew from protecting goods at sea.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 enseurer 意为「使确定」，商业义从保护海上货物发展而来。

senses.title: Make certain
senses.definition: to make something certain to happen, especially by taking action in advance
senses.definitionCN: 尤指通过事先行动使某事必定发生
senses.example: Book early to insure yourself a seat by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 早点预订，确保给自己留一个靠窗的座位。
senses.why: This sense is close to ensure and dominates in American writing.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项与 ensure 相近，在美式写作中占主导。

senses.title: Promise firmly
senses.definition: to state firmly that something is true or will be done
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地声明某事为真或将被做到
senses.example: He insured me that the parts would arrive on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 他向我保证零件周一会到。
senses.why: The old promise sense survives in legal and formal speech.
senses.whyCN: 古老的「承诺」义仍存在于法律与正式语体中。

intro.en: Insure descends from Latin securus through Old French enseurer, and entered English with the sea trade.
intro.cn: insure 由拉丁语 securus 经古法语 enseurer 传来，随海上贸易进入英语。

items.en: Securus, "free from care", was built from se- "without" and cura "care".
items.cn: securus「无忧的」由 se-「无」与 cura「忧虑」构成。

items.en: Securare meant to set free from worry or to give a pledge.
items.cn: securare 意为「使无忧」，也指给出担保。

items.en: Enseurer "to make sure" carried the pledge sense into French commerce.
items.cn: enseurer「使确定」把担保义带入法语商业用语。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English merchants wrote ensuren for goods shipped overseas.
items.cn: 十六世纪的英国商人用 ensuren 指海外运输的货物。

items.en: Spelling settled as insure, and American usage kept it also in the sense of ensure.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 insure，美式英语还用它表示 ensure 的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the pledge root; the near-meaning group holds words about making things certain.
note.cn: 形近组共享「担保」这一词根；近义组收表示「使确定」的词。

entries.definition: To make certain that something happens.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「确保」，强调使某事发生。

entries.definition: To tell someone confidently so as to remove doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使某人确信」，强调打消对方疑虑。

entries.definition: The contract or money behind such protection.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保险」，指其背后的合同或费用。

entries.definition: To promise formally to answer for a result.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「担保」，正式承诺为结果负责。

entries.definition: To obtain something after effort, or to fasten it.
To keep someone or something from harm.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「保护」，侧重免受伤害。

normalIntro.en: The hooks work from the sure inside insure and from the phrases it keeps company with.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从 insure 中间那个 sure「确定」出发，并借助它的常见搭配。

normal.en: in plus sure: put your goods in a sure place.
normal.cn: in 加 sure：把东西放进稳妥之处。

normal.en: Insure the parcel against damage, insure that the door is locked.
normal.cn: 给包裹投保防损，也确保门已锁好。

normal.en: American writers often use insure where British writers use ensure.
normal.cn: 美式作者常用 insure，而英式作者用 ensure。

normal.en: Only the insured can claim from the insurer.
normal.cn: 只有被保险人才能向保险公司索赔。

normal.en: Insure what you cannot afford to lose.
normal.cn: 给那些丢了赔不起的东西投保。

abstract.en: To insure is to buy a calm night from a company.
abstract.cn: 投保就是向公司买一个安稳的夜晚。

abstract.en: The word carries two jobs: cover the risk, and remove the doubt.
abstract.cn: 这个词承担两份工作：兜住风险，也消除疑虑。

abstract.en: A careful traveller insures the trip before feeling excited about it.
abstract.cn: 细心的旅客先给旅程投保，再为它兴奋。

examples.en: Make sure you insure the laptop before the trip.
examples.cn: 出发前一定要给笔记本电脑投保。

examples.en: The club insured its players against injury.
examples.cn: 俱乐部为球员投保了伤病险。

examples.en: Hard practice will insure a better result next term.
examples.cn: 刻苦练习能确保下学期有更好的成绩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因输尔」——怕因为输了而受损，先去投保

root: 拉丁语 cura「忧虑」→ securus「无忧的」→ securare「使无忧、担保」→ 古法语 enseurer「使确定」→ 英语 insure。与 insurance、ensure、assure 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: buying cover, making something certain, and giving a firm promise.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：买东西的保障、使某事确定，以及郑重承诺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hand something valuable over and get back a written pledge.
core.cn: 核心意象：把贵重东西交出去，换回一纸担保。

branches.en: THE PARCEL: goods are covered against loss before shipping.
branches.cn: 包裹这条线：货物在发运前被投保防损。

branches.en: THE EARLY BOOKING: acting ahead makes the seat certain.
branches.cn: 早订这条线：提前行动让座位变得确定。

branches.en: THE FORMAL WORD: a spoken pledge in legal or polite speech.
branches.cn: 正式承诺这条线：法律或客套话里的郑重保证。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses remove worry about what might happen.
branches.cn: 连接线：两个义项都在消除对可能发生之事的担忧。

branches.en: THE LINK: cover and promise both rest on someone else's word.
branches.cn: 连接线：保险与承诺都建立在别人的一句话上。

intro.en: Insure lines up in-, the root sur- from securus, and the verb ending -e.
intro.cn: insure 可拆为 in-、来自 securus 的词根 sur- 与动词词尾 -e。

latinIntro.en: Latin securus and securare are recorded; the reconstructed layer lies further back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 securus 与 securare 均有记录，重构层在更早的阶段。

items.example: It marks entry into a safe state.
The root shows clearly in assure and secure.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根在 assure 与 secure 中很明显。

items.example: It is the verb behind the French form.
items.exampleCN: 它是法语形式背后的拉丁动词。

items.example: The French form gave English the spelling.
items.exampleCN: 法语形式给出了英语的拼写。
另一个单独借入的近亲。

definition_en: in a way that shows anger
core_image: 门被用力带上，脚步声急促远去
scene: 她把手里的文件往桌上一放，转身就走，没说一句话。 She left the room angrily without a word.
sceneCN: 这里 angrily 是「愤怒地」（第 1 个义项：以显出怒气的样子做某事）；句意是她一言不发地愤怒离开房间。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：更生气的，angry 的比较级
形容词：最生气的，angry 的最高级

senses.title: In an angry manner
senses.definition: doing something in a way that clearly shows anger
senses.definitionCN: 以明显显出怒气的方式做某事
senses.example: She left the room angrily without a word.
senses.exampleCN: 她一言不发地愤然离开房间。
senses.why: The -ly form of angry describes the manner of an action, so angrily tells you how someone spoke, looked, or moved, not how they felt inside.
senses.whyCN: angry 的 -ly 形式描述动作方式，所以 angrily 说明某人说话、看人或走动的样子，而不是内心的感受。

senses.title: With violent force, in description
senses.titleCN: 猛烈地；狂暴地（拟人描写）
senses.definition: used of wind, water, or weather that seems to act with anger in literary description
senses.definitionCN: 文学描写中形容风、水或天气仿佛带着怒气般猛烈
senses.example: The wind blew angrily through the empty streets.
senses.exampleCN: 风在空荡的街道上怒号。
senses.why: Writers transfer human anger to nature, so angrily can describe a storm's force as if it were a temper.
senses.whyCN: 作家把人的愤怒移到自然身上，于是 angrily 可以把风暴的猛烈写成仿佛有脾气。

intro.en: Angrily is angry with its y changed to i and an -ly added.
intro.cn: angrily 就是 angry 把词尾 y 改成 i 再加 -ly。

items.en: angr meant 'grief, distress', the distant source of the family.
items.cn: angr 意为「悲痛、痛苦」，是这一词族的远源。

items.en: anger shifted from distress to wrath.
items.cn: anger 从痛苦转向暴怒。

items.en: The adjective angry was formed with -y, meaning 'full of anger'.
items.cn: 形容词 angry 由 -y 构成，意为「充满怒气的」。

items.en: The adverb angrily appears, with y changing to i before -ly.
items.cn: 副词 angrily 出现，y 在 -ly 前变为 i。

items.en: Angrily is now the standard adverb for speech and behaviour that shows anger.
items.cn: 现代 angrily 是表示言语与行为显露怒气的标准副词。

note.en: The look-alike group is the anger family; the near-meaning group gives other angry adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组是 anger 词族；近义组给出其他表示愤怒的副词。

entries.definition: feeling anger
the feeling of rage
more angry
with wild anger
in a mildly annoyed way
with strong feeling

normalIntro.en: Angry plus -ly, with y turned into i: angrily.
normalIntro.cn: angry 加 -ly，y 变 i：angrily。

normal.en: Adjectives ending in y change y to i before -ly.
normal.cn: 以 y 结尾的形容词加 -ly 时把 y 变成 i。

normal.en: Angrily describes the action, anger the feeling.
normal.cn: angrily 描述动作，anger 描述情绪。

normal.en: Speak angrily is the most common collocation.
normal.cn: speak angrily 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: Do not write angryly; the i is required.
normal.cn: 不要写成 angryly，必须用 i。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AN-gri-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AN-gri-ly。

abstract.en: Picture a door slammed hard.
abstract.cn: 想象门被重重带上。

abstract.en: See papers dropped on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象文件被拍在桌上。

abstract.en: Hear wind rattling an empty street.
abstract.cn: 听到风在空街上作响。

examples.en: He replied angrily that the decision was unfair.
examples.cn: 他气愤地回答说这个决定不公平。

examples.en: The crowd shouted angrily at the referee.
examples.cn: 人群愤怒地朝裁判喊叫。

examples.en: She stared angrily at the broken window.
examples.cn: 她气愤地盯着破碎的窗户。

dict_mnemonic.text: angry（生气的）加 -ly（地），y 变 i：愤怒地。

root: 由形容词 angry 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，y 在词尾前变为 i；angry 来自中古英语 anger 加 -y，而 anger 源自古北欧语 angr「悲痛」，词义后转为愤怒。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb covers human behaviour and, in literature, the violence of weather.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词既写人的行为，也在文学中写天气的猛烈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slammed door and quick footsteps.
core.cn: 核心意象：被摔上的门与急促的脚步。

branches.en: replying in anger
branches.cn: 气愤地回答

branches.en: shouting at a referee
branches.cn: 朝裁判怒吼

branches.en: leaving without a word
branches.cn: 一言不发地离开

branches.en: wind tearing through streets
branches.cn: 风在街道上怒号

branches.en: waves beating the shore
branches.cn: 浪愤怒地拍岸

intro.en: A regular -ly adverb, useful for showing how an emotion surfaces in action.
intro.cn: 这是规则的 -ly 副词，用于表现情绪如何显露在动作中。

latinIntro.en: The base is Norse rather than Latin, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自北欧语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁词条留空。

definition_en: extremely large in size, amount or degree
core_image: 站在山脚仰望那面占据整片天空的岩壁
scene: 火车穿过荒原开了六个小时，窗外仍是一片同一种草色。 The plain looked immense, and the passengers stopped talking to watch it pass.
sceneCN: 这里 immense 是「巨大的、广大的」（第 1 个义项：面积或规模极大），句意是平原看上去无边无际，乘客们停下谈话望着它掠过。画面里有六小时不变的同色草原。

pos.zh: 形容词：巨大的、极大的、广大的

senses.title: Very large in size
senses.definition: far larger than usual, hard to take in at one look
senses.definitionCN: 远大于寻常，一眼难以收进视野
senses.example: An immense cliff rose above the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 一道巨大的崖壁耸立在港口上方。
senses.why: The Latin root means measured, and the prefix denies it: immense is what cannot be measured.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「度量」，前缀加以否定：immense 就是量不出来的东西。

senses.title: Very great in amount or degree
senses.definition: used of feelings, pressure or wealth on an extreme scale
senses.definitionCN: 形容感受、压力或财富达到极端程度
senses.example: The team worked under immense pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队承受着巨大的压力。
senses.why: Anything beyond measure can be weight or emotion as easily as rock, so the word moved from space to feeling.
senses.whyCN: 凡超出度量之物，既可以是岩石，也可以是压力或情绪，于是词义由空间移向感受。

senses.title: Very impressive or enjoyable
senses.definition: used informally in British speech to praise something warmly
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中热情称赞某物
senses.example: The concert last night was immense.
senses.exampleCN: 昨晚的音乐会太棒了。
senses.why: Young speech reuses extreme-size words for praise, so an immense crowd becomes an immense evening.
senses.whyCN: 年轻人的口语常借表示「极大」的词来赞美，于是 immense crowd 变成 immense evening。

intro.en: Immense carries a Latin word for measuring, cancelled by a negative prefix: it names what has no measure.
intro.cn: immense 含一个拉丁语的「度量」词，被否定前缀抵消：它命名的是无法计量之物。

items.en: Metiri meant to measure, and mensus was its past participle, measured.
items.cn: 拉丁语 metiri 意为测量，过去分词 mensus 即「量过的」。

items.en: Immansus or immensus described what was unmeasured and beyond reckoning.
items.cn: immanus 或 immensus 形容未加丈量、难以估算之物。

items.en: Poets used immensus of the sea, night and the heavens.
items.cn: 诗人用 immensus 形容大海、黑夜与天空。

items.en: French carried immense, and it kept the grand, slightly poetic air.
items.cn: 法语沿承 immense，仍带宏大而略富诗意的气韵。

items.en: English adopted it, later extending it to pressure, wealth and informal praise.
items.cn: 英语引入后，进一步扩展到压力、财富与口语赞美。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same measure root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for great size.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「度量」词根的词；近义组收其他表示庞大的词。

entries.definition: Very much, the adverb formed from this adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 非常、极大地，由本词构成的副词。

entries.definition: The quality of being vast.
To find the size of something, the root that the prefix denies.
entries.definitionCN: 量出大小，正是前缀所否定的那个词根。

entries.definition: Very big, the most common word of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 非常大，这组里最常用的词。

entries.definition: Extremely wide, used of areas and amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 极其辽阔，多用于面积与数量。

entries.definition: Beyond normal size, literally out of rule.
entries.definitionCN: 超出常规尺寸，字面是「出格」。

normalIntro.en: The hooks rest on the measure root and the cancelled prefix, and on trains crossing endless plains.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子立在「度量」词根与被抵消的前缀上，也立在穿越荒原的火车上。

normal.en: Im- is not, mens is measure, so immense is unmeasurable.
normal.cn: im- 是不，mens 是度量，所以 immense 就是「量不出来」。

normal.en: The same mens sits inside measure and dimension.
normal.cn: 同一个 mens 也藏在 measure 与 dimension 里。

normal.en: Two syllables, stress the second: im-MENSE.
normal.cn: 两个音节，重音在后：im-MENSE。

normal.en: Immense pressure and immense wealth show the word is about scale, not only rock.
normal.cn: 巨大压力与巨额财富说明这个词讲的是尺度，不只是石头。

normal.en: Add -ly and immense becomes a strong very: immensely grateful.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 就变成加强版的 very：immensely grateful。

abstract.en: The word measures by refusing to measure, the same trick as calling a sea unending.
abstract.cn: 这个词用拒绝度量来表示度量之大，与称大海无边是同一种手法。

abstract.en: Anything immense forces the eye to move, so the word always implies a small viewer.
abstract.cn: 凡巨大之物都迫使眼睛转动，所以这个词总隐含着一个渺小的观看者。

abstract.en: Feelings borrow their size from space, which is why we call grief immense and not merely strong.
abstract.cn: 情感借空间的尺度来说大小，所以我们说悲伤巨大，而不只说悲伤强烈。

examples.en: The desert stretched out beneath them, immense and silent.
examples.cn: 沙漠在他们下方延展开来，宽广而寂静。

examples.en: She has brought immense energy to the project.
examples.cn: 她为这个项目投入了巨大的精力。

examples.en: We are immensely grateful for your help.
examples.cn: 我们对你的帮助极为感激。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 不 + mens 度量 + e——量不出来的，即巨大无边的

root: 拉丁语 metiri「测量」（分词 mensus）加否定前缀 in- 成 immensus「无法丈量的」，经法语 immense 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: huge in space, extreme in amount, and immense in colloquial praise.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：空间上巨大、数量或程度上极端，以及口语中的「极好」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cliff wall taking up the entire sky above a small climber.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道占据整片天空的岩壁，崖下是渺小的攀登者。

branches.en: THE LANDSCAPE LINE: cliffs and plains defeat the eye.
branches.cn: 风景线：崖壁与原野让眼睛投降。

branches.en: THE PRESSURE LINE: emotions and workloads are called immense too.
branches.cn: 压力线：情绪与工作量也称 immense。

branches.en: THE SLANG LINE: young British speakers praise with it.
branches.cn: 俚语线：英国年轻人用它赞美。

branches.en: THE SCALE LINE: the word always answers how much, never how.
branches.cn: 尺度线：这个词永远回答「多大」，从不回答「怎样」。

branches.en: THE FEELING LINE: its two softer senses both concern attitude.
branches.cn: 感受线：两个较软的义项都与态度有关。

intro.en: Immense is a negative prefix on the Latin measure root, with -ly and -ity forms built on top.
intro.cn: immense 是否定前缀加拉丁语度量词根，上面再长出 -ly 与 -ity 形式。

latinIntro.en: Metiri and its participle mensus are standard Latin, and immensus is a common poetic word.
latinIntro.cn: metiri 及其分词 mensus 是标准拉丁成分，immensus 则是常见的诗语。

items.example: An immense wave broke over the boat.
The immensity of the sky frightened her.
Measure the room before buying the rug.
items.exampleCN: 买地毯前先量一下房间。

items.example: It is only two dimensions on paper.
items.exampleCN: 在纸上它只有两个维度。

items.example: Pay should be commensurate with skill.

definition_en: to breathe out slowly and audibly, or the sound of doing so
core_image: 一个人肩膀一沉，长长地吐出一口气
scene: 读完信，她叹了口气，把信放下。 She sighed and put down the letter.
sceneCN: 这里 sigh 是「叹气」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她叹了口气，把信放下。

senses.title: To breathe out in this way
senses.definition: to breathe out slowly and audibly, often from sadness or relief
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而带声地呼气，常因悲伤或宽慰
senses.example: She sighed and put down the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 她叹了口气，把信放下。
senses.why: This is the action sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是动作义项。

senses.title: The sound of a sigh
senses.definition: the sound made when someone sighs
senses.definitionCN: 人叹气时发出的声音
senses.example: A long sigh came from the back row.
senses.exampleCN: 后排传来一声长长的叹息。
senses.why: The action and its sound share one word.
senses.whyCN: 动作和声音共用一个词。

intro.en: Sigh is an imitative word for a long breath.
intro.cn: sigh 是模仿长呼气声音的词。

items.en: Sican meant to sigh.
items.cn: sican 意为叹气。

items.en: The form became sighen.
items.cn: 词形演变为 sighen。

items.en: The spelling settled as sigh.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 sigh。

items.en: The noun use named the sound.
items.cn: 名词用法用来指叹息声。

items.en: The phrase sigh of relief became common.
items.cn: 短语 sigh of relief（松了一口气）变得常用。

note.en: Sigh is compared with similar-looking words and with other breath sounds.
note.cn: 把 sigh 与形近词以及其他呼吸声词作比较。

normal.en: He sighed with relief.

normal.en: She sighs before speaking.
normal.cn: 她说话前先叹了口气。

normal.en: They sighed over the lost chance.
normal.cn: 他们为错过的机会叹息。

abstract.en: A sigh is a sentence without words.
abstract.cn: 叹息是一句没有词的句子。

abstract.en: Breath carries what speech cannot.
abstract.cn: 呼吸带走了言语带不走的东西。

abstract.en: Every sigh lets a little weight go.
abstract.cn: 每一次叹息都放下一分重量。

root: 源自古英语 sīcan（叹气），核心义「长长地吐气」。

sensesIntro.en: Sigh means to breathe out audibly, or the sound of that breath.
sensesIntro.cn: sigh 意为出声地叹气，或指叹息声。

core.en: A slow breath released with sound.
core.cn: 带声慢慢放出的一口气。

branches.en: The sound itself carries the feeling.
branches.cn: 声音本身就带着情绪。

intro.en: Sigh forms a small family of breath and emotion words.
intro.cn: sigh 构成一个表示呼吸与情绪的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Sigh is Germanic; Latin suspirare, to sigh deeply, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: sigh 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 suspirare（深深叹息）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She sighs when she is tired.

items.meaning: the act or sound of sighing

items.example: We breathed a sigh of relief.
Do not sigh over the past.

definition_en: the act of making something start working or become chemically active
core_image: 一枚钥匙插进锁孔，指示灯由红转绿
scene: 警报被激活后，整栋楼的人都醒了。 The activation of the alarm woke the whole building.
sceneCN: 这里的 activation 是「启动」（第 1 个义项：使设备开始工作）；句意是警报启动惊醒了全楼。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「激活；启动」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「活跃的；活性的」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「激活剂」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「活动；活性」

senses.title: Starting a device or system
senses.definition: the act of making a machine, account or system begin to work
senses.definitionCN: 使机器、账户或系统开始工作的行为
senses.example: Activation of the card takes a single phone call.
senses.exampleCN: 激活这张卡只需打一个电话。
senses.why: The verb activate means to make active, and the noun names that switch from dormant to working.
senses.whyCN: 动词 activate 意为「使进入活动状态」，名词便指从休眠转为运转的那一下。

senses.title: Making a substance chemically active
senses.definition: the process of giving a molecule or cell the energy to react
senses.definitionCN: 使分子或细胞获得反应所需能量的过程
senses.example: The activation of the enzyme requires a small amount of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这种酶的活化需要少量热量。
senses.why: In chemistry the same switch is pushed at the molecular level: a particle goes from inert to ready.
senses.whyCN: 在化学里，同一个开关被按在分子层面：微粒从惰性变为待发。

intro.en: The noun is built on the Latin act root with a suffix meaning to make.
intro.cn: 这个名词建在拉丁语 act 词根上，带一个表示「使……」的后缀。

items.en: agere meant to drive or to do.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动或做。

items.en: activus described something able to act.
items.cn: activus 形容能够行动的东西。

items.en: active entered English as an adjective of doing.
items.cn: active 作为表示行动、活跃的形容词进入英语。

items.en: activate and activation spread with technology and chemistry.
items.cn: activate 与 activation 随技术与化学的发展而普及。

items.en: the noun now covers software keys, alarms and enzymes.
items.cn: 如今这个名词涵盖软件密钥、警报器与酶。

note.en: The first group is the activate family; the second is other words for starting something.
note.cn: 第一组是 activate 词族；第二组是别的表示启动的词。

entries.definition: to make something start working
working or doing things
a thing that starts a process
the state of being busy or working
the process of beginning to operate
to cause something to begin
the act of turning on power
the arousing of activity

normalIntro.en: active plus -ate plus -ion is the whole recipe.
normalIntro.cn: active 加 -ate 再加 -ion，就是全部配方。

normal.en: activation is to active what creation is to create.
normal.cn: activation 之于 active，正如 creation 之于 create。

normal.en: activation code is the phrase on every software card.
normal.cn: activation code 是每张软件卡上的说法。

normal.en: activation energy is the barrier a reaction must climb.
normal.cn: activation energy 是反应必须翻过的门槛。

normal.en: the verb activate keeps the same stress shift as the noun.
normal.cn: 动词 activate 与名词的重音位置相互对应。

normal.en: an account, an alarm and an enzyme can all be activated.
normal.cn: 账户、警报器与酶都可以被激活。

abstract.en: See a key turn and a red light become green.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙一转，红灯变绿。

abstract.en: Picture a dormant enzyme waking when warmth arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象惰性的酶遇到温度便苏醒。

abstract.en: Think of a phone screen lighting up at a first touch.
abstract.cn: 想象手机屏幕在第一次触碰时亮起。

examples.en: Activation of the new account takes only a minute.
examples.cn: 新账户的激活只需一分钟。

examples.en: The activation of the alarm startled the whole street.
examples.cn: 警报的启动惊动了整条街。

examples.en: Heat lowers the activation energy of the reaction.
examples.cn: 热量降低了反应的活化能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克提维申」——阿克把钥匙一插，系统立刻「提」起精神开始运转。

root: 由 activate（使活动）加名词后缀 -ion 构成；activate 源自拉丁语 activus（能行动的），词根 agere 意为驱动、做。

sensesIntro.en: The same switch works on machines and on molecules.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个开关，既管机器，也管分子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dormant thing receiving the spark of motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：沉睡之物接到一点动力。

branches.en: a card or account coming to life
branches.cn: 卡片或账户开始生效

branches.en: an enzyme gaining the power to react
branches.cn: 酶获得反应能力

branches.en: an alarm sounding after being set
branches.cn: 设好的警报开始鸣响

branches.en: a neuron firing after stimulation
branches.cn: 神经元受刺激后放电

branches.cn: 技术与化学共用一个「启动」词

intro.en: The act root plus a make-verb ending and a noun ending build the word.

latinIntro.en: The root agere, to drive, also gives agent and agenda.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 agere（驱动）也给出 agent 与 agenda。

definition_en: to say words for someone to write down, or to order something firmly
core_image: 一个人在屋里边走边说，旁边的人低头飞快记录
scene: 老编辑在屋里来回走，一句一句念，年轻助手埋头记。 The manager dictated a short letter to his assistant.
sceneCN: 这里 dictate 指「口述」（第 1 个义项：念出文字让人记下来）；句意是经理向助手口述了一封短信。

senses.title: Say words to be written
senses.definition: to speak words aloud so that someone else can write them down
senses.definitionCN: 把话念出来，让别人记录下来
senses.example: The manager dictated a short letter to his assistant.
senses.exampleCN: 经理向助手口述了一封短信。
senses.why: One mouth can keep moving while another hand does the slow work.
senses.whyCN: 一张嘴可以一直说，另一只手去做那件慢活。

senses.title: Order with authority
senses.definition: to tell someone what to do in a forceful and official way
senses.definitionCN: 以强硬而正式的方式吩咐别人做什么
senses.example: The general dictated the terms of the surrender.
senses.exampleCN: 将军规定了投降的条件。
senses.why: When the words carry power, the listener has no pen to refuse with.
senses.whyCN: 当话里带着权力，听的人就没有一支可以拒绝的笔。

senses.title: Control or decide
senses.definition: to control or decide what happens
senses.definitionCN: 控制或决定事情会怎么发生
senses.example: Demand often dictates what a factory produces.
senses.exampleCN: 需求常常决定工厂生产什么。
senses.why: An invisible force can still write the script everyone follows.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的力量，也能写下所有人照着念的剧本。

intro.en: Dictate comes from Latin dictare, to say repeatedly or to prescribe, a stronger form of dicere, to say.
intro.cn: dictate 来自拉丁语 dictare（反复说、规定），是 dicere（说）的加强形式。

items.en: Dicere meant simply to say or to tell.
items.cn: dicere 就是「说」或「告诉」。

items.en: Dictare meant to say again and again, so that others could take it down.
items.cn: dictare 指一遍遍地说，好让别人记下来。

items.en: It also meant to order, because a repeated word carries authority.
items.cn: 它也指命令，因为反复说出的话自带权威。

items.en: English dictate kept both the writing and the ordering senses.
items.cn: 英语 dictate 同时保留了记录与命令这两层意思。

items.en: It now also describes forces, needs and circumstances that decide things.
items.cn: 如今它也形容决定事情的力量、需求与形势。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dict stem, while the meaning group moves from commanding to prescribing and instructing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 dict 这个词干，近义组则从命令走到规定与指示。

entries.definition: the act of speaking words to be written
entries.definitionCN: 念出文字让人记录的行为

entries.definition: a ruler with total power
entries.definitionCN: 掌握全部权力的统治者

entries.definition: a book listing words and meanings
to order someone to do something
to state what must be done
to tell someone how to do something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a voice walking around a room and end with a market deciding what a factory makes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从在屋里走来走去的声音开始，落到决定工厂生产什么的市场。

normal.en: Dictare is to say it again, so the other hand has time to catch up.
normal.cn: dictare 就是再说一遍，好让另一只手跟得上。

normal.en: The same verb gives order to a clerk and orders to an army.
normal.cn: 同一个动词，既给职员派活，也给军队下令。

normal.en: A letter can be dictated; a price can be dictated; both come from above.
normal.cn: 信可以被口述，价格可以被规定，两者都来自上方。

normal.en: Demand holds the pen even when nobody is in the room.
normal.cn: 即使屋里没人，需求也握着那支笔。

normal.en: A dictator is simply a voice that stopped listening.
normal.cn: 独裁者不过是一个不再听的嗓音。

abstract.en: Picture a man pacing beside a window.
abstract.cn: 想象一个男人在窗边来回踱步。

abstract.en: Picture a pen moving without looking up.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔头也不抬地移动。

abstract.en: Picture a long table where terms are read aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，条件被逐条念出来。

examples.en: The general dictated the terms of the surrender.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dictate 记成「迪克推特」：dict 是说，-ate 是动词，把话推出去说给人记，就是口述与命令。

root: 来自拉丁语 dictare，是 dicere（说）的加强形式，本义是一遍遍地说，好让别人记下来，也指以权威口气规定。十六世纪进入英语，既保留口述义，也发展出命令与支配义。

sensesIntro.en: From a voice slowly feeding a pen, to a voice that expects obedience, to an unseen force writing the rules.
sensesIntro.cn: 从慢慢喂给笔的一把声音，到期待服从的一把声音，再到写下规则的看不见的力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice pacing the room while a hand hurries to keep up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把声音在屋里踱步，一只手忙着跟上。

branches.en: The first sense is the voice serving the writer.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是声音在为记录者服务。

branches.en: The second sense is the voice that no longer asks.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是那把不再询问的声音。

branches.en: The third sense is a force that writes without a mouth.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是没有嘴却在写字的某种力量。

branches.en: The same steady speech can serve or command.
branches.cn: 同一种平稳的说话，可以服务，也可以命令。

branches.en: What is commanded and what is decided end up as one rule.
branches.cn: 被命令的与被决定的，最后成了同一条规则。

intro.en: Dictate has a family built on saying, repeating and laying down the law.
intro.cn: dictate 有一族词，建在说、反复说与定规矩之上。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin dicere, to say, and dictare repeats it with authority.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 dicere（说），dictare 则带着权威把它反复说出。

definition_zh: 谦虚的；适度的；朴素的；端庄的
definition_en: not boasting about one's own abilities or achievements; not large in amount or size; simple and not expensive; decent in dress and behaviour
core_image: 一个人站在人群边上，把自己的成绩轻轻往身后放
scene: 颁奖结束后，年轻人把证书先递给身边的老师，说这份功劳多半是老师给的。 The young engineer stayed modest even after the whole team praised her design.
sceneCN: 这里 modest 是「谦虚的」（第 1 个义项：不夸耀自己的能力与成绩）；句意为整个团队称赞她的设计之后，这位年轻工程师仍然保持谦虚。画面里能想见：颁奖台、递出去的证书、站在一旁的老师。

pos.zh: 谦虚的；适度的；朴素的；端庄的

collocations.zh: 微薄的收入；不宽裕的经济条件

derivatives.zh: 由 modest 改词尾为 -y 构成，义为「谦虚；适度；朴素」
由 modest 加 -ly 构成，义为「谦虚地；适度地」
由否定前缀 im- 加 modest 构成，义为「不谦虚的；自夸的」
由 im- 加 modesty 构成，义为「自负；不谦逊」

senses.title: Not boasting about one's abilities or achievements
senses.definition: not talking proudly about your own abilities, successes or importance
senses.definitionCN: 不骄傲地谈论自己的能力、成绩或地位
senses.example: She is modest about the prize and keeps praising her teammates.
senses.exampleCN: 她对这个奖很谦虚，一直在夸队友。
senses.why: Latin modestus was built on modus, a measure; a person who keeps inside the measure does not inflate the space they take up in the room.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modestus 建立在 modus（尺度）之上；一个守在尺度之内的人，不会把自己在众人面前占的位置吹大。

senses.title: Small in amount, size or degree
senses.definition: not large in amount, size or degree, often pleasantly so
senses.definitionCN: 数量、规模或程度上不大，常带「还算合适」的意味
senses.example: Sales rose by a modest seven percent this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年销售额小幅上升了七个点。
senses.why: The same idea of staying inside a measure applies to numbers: a modest rise is one that does not overshoot the expected line.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「守在尺度内」的想法也能用在数字上：modest 的增长就是没有越过预期那条线的增长。

senses.title: Simple and not expensive
senses.definition: plain and simple, not showy or expensive, especially of clothes, homes or meals
senses.definitionCN: 朴素简单而不张扬、不昂贵，尤指衣着、住所或饭菜
senses.example: They live in a modest flat near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在车站附近一套朴素的公寓里。
senses.why: A house that refuses to show off its cost is following the same rule as a person who refuses to show off a trophy.
senses.whyCN: 一座不肯炫耀造价的房子，遵守的规则和一个人不肯炫耀奖杯完全一样。

senses.title: Decent in dress and behaviour, not revealing
senses.definition: of clothes or behaviour, avoiding anything that draws sexual attention
senses.definitionCN: 指衣着或举止避开会引起性方面注意的东西
senses.example: The school asks students to wear modest clothing.
senses.exampleCN: 学校要求学生穿端庄的衣着。
senses.why: Here the measure is social: clothing that stays within what a situation allows covers the body instead of inviting stares.
senses.whyCN: 这里的尺度是社会性的：守在场合适度的衣着遮住身体，而不招来盯视。

intro.en: Modest goes back to a Latin word for keeping to a measure, and French passed it into English as a word about restraint rather than size.
intro.cn: modest 可追到拉丁语中「守尺度」的说法，法语把它传入英语时，谈的是节制，而不是大小。

items.en: Modus meant a measure, a limit or a way of doing something, and it is the root behind mode, moderate and modest.
items.cn: modus 意为尺度、限度或做事的门径，是 mode、moderate 与 modest 共同的词根。

items.en: Modestus described someone who stayed within due measure, sober in manner and free of swagger.
items.cn: modestus 形容守分寸的人：举止有节、不张狂。

items.en: Modestia named that quality itself, the habit of not claiming more than one's share.
items.cn: modestia 指这种品质本身，即不多占、不越界的习惯。

items.en: French took the adjective as modeste and used it for people, manners and later for plain, unshowy things.
items.cn: 法语把形容词写作 modeste，先用于人和举止，后来也用于朴素、不张扬的事物。

items.en: English extended the word from humble speech to small amounts, simple homes and decent clothing.
items.cn: 英语把这个词从谦逊的言谈扩展到小额数量、简朴住所与端庄衣着。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin measure root and its English family; the near-meaning group gathers words for humility, smallness and plainness.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「尺度」词根及其英语词族展开；近义组收表示谦逊、少量与朴素的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the habit of not boasting, and for plainness in dress.
entries.definitionCN: 不夸耀的习惯，也指衣着朴素；是 modest 的名词形式。

entries.definition: In a humble or moderate way.
Boastful, or too revealing in dress.
entries.definitionCN: 自夸的，或衣着过于暴露的。

entries.definition: Keeping within limits, neither too much nor too little.
entries.definitionCN: 守在中庸之内的；不过分也不欠缺的。

entries.definition: A way or manner of doing something, from the same Latin measure word.
entries.definitionCN: 做事的方式、门径，来自同一个表示尺度的拉丁词。

entries.definition: Having a low opinion of your own importance.
entries.definitionCN: 对自己的重要性评价低；谦逊的。

entries.definition: Neither very large nor very small.
entries.definitionCN: 既不大也不小的；中等的。

entries.definition: Simple, with no decoration or display.
entries.definitionCN: 简单的，没有装饰或炫耀的。

entries.definition: Not drawing attention to yourself or your merits.
entries.definitionCN: 不引人注意自己的功劳的；不摆架子的。

normalIntro.en: The word grows out of a Latin word for measure, and its whole family keeps asking whether someone or something stays inside its proper size.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词长在拉丁语表示「尺度」的词上，整个词族反复在问：人或者事物有没有守在自己该有的大小里。

normal.en: Modus is Latin for a measure or limit, so modest begins as a judgement about staying inside the line.
normal.cn: modus 是拉丁语的「尺度、限度」，所以 modest 起初是对「有没有守在线内」的判断。

normal.en: Modesty swaps the -est ending for -y, the same pattern as honest and honesty.
normal.cn: modesty 把 -est 词尾换成 -y，和 honest 变 honesty 是同一种构词方式。

normal.en: im- can negate: immodest is the person who claims more than their measure allows.
normal.cn: im- 可以表否定：immodest 就是占了超出自己尺度的位置的人。

normal.en: Modest about praise, modest rise, modest flat: one word measures claims, numbers and housing alike.
normal.cn: 对赞美谦虚、小幅增长、朴素公寓：同一个词在衡量说法、数字和住处。

normal.en: In clothing, modest marks what stays covered instead of inviting attention.
normal.cn: 用在衣着上，modest 标记的是遮蔽得宜、不招来注视的那种穿法。

abstract.en: Think of a person who could take up the whole stage but chooses one small square of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人本可以占满整个舞台，却只挑了一小块地方站。

abstract.en: A modest number behaves like a polite guest: it arrives without filling the room.
abstract.cn: 一个不大的数字像有礼貌的客人：来了，但不把屋子塞满。

abstract.en: Measuring is the quiet act behind the word, and every sense is a different ruler.
abstract.cn: 「量」是这个词背后的动作，而每个义项都换了一把不同的尺子。

examples.en: She is modest about the prize and keeps praising her teammates.
examples.cn: 她对这个奖很谦虚，一直在夸队友。

examples.en: They live in a modest flat near the station.
examples.cn: 他们住在车站附近一套朴素的公寓里。

examples.en: The school asks students to wear modest clothing.
examples.cn: 学校要求学生穿端庄的衣着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩的」——骑摩的的师傅挣得不多，日子过得朴实，也不吹牛；modest 就是适度、朴素、谦虚。

root: 拉丁语 modus（尺度、限度）派生出 modestus（守分寸的），再经法语 modeste 进入英语；同族词都与尺度、节制有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is staying inside a measure; the senses apply that measure to claims about oneself, to quantity, to possessions and to the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是守在尺度之内；义项把同一把尺子依次用在自我评价、数量、财物和身体上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing at the edge of a group, quietly putting her own achievement behind her back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在人群边上，把自己的成绩悄悄藏到身后。

branches.en: a winner who names the people who helped
branches.cn: 获奖者说出帮助过自己的人

branches.en: a sales chart rising by one small step
branches.cn: 销售曲线只抬高一小格

branches.en: a plain flat with bare walls and one lamp
branches.cn: 白墙素灯的一间小屋

branches.en: a meal served without decoration or display
branches.cn: 一顿不作摆盘的饭菜

branches.en: a school rule about sleeves and hemlines
branches.cn: 关于袖长与下摆的校规

intro.en: A Latin measure word, a quality noun, a French adjective and three English endings carry modest from a ruler to a manner of speech, a size and a dress code.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「尺度」词、一个表品质的名词、一个法语形容词和三个英语词尾，把 modest 从一把尺子带到了说话方式、尺寸和衣着规范。

latinIntro.en: Modus and modestia are recorded Latin words, and the adjective modestus is built on them; the family carries the idea of a limit.
latinIntro.cn: modus 与 modestia 都是有记录的拉丁词，形容词 modestus 由它们构成；这一族词都带着「限度」的观念。

items.meaningCN: 形容词词尾：具有……性质的

definition_en: to give someone the desire or confidence to do something, or to be the cause of an idea
core_image: 一口气吹进原本微弱的小火苗，火焰一下窜高起来
scene: 音乐教室里几个学生低着头，不敢开口。 Her first teacher inspired her to become a writer.
sceneCN: 这里 inspire 是「激励、鼓舞」（第 1 个义项：使人产生做某事的愿望或信心），句意是她第一位老师激励她成为作家。画面里可想象的物件：钢琴、谱架、向外窜起的火苗。

pos.zh: 动词：鼓舞；激励；启发；激起

derivatives.zh: 由本词换后缀构成，义为「灵感；鼓舞」
由现在分词构成，义为「鼓舞人心的」
由过去分词构成，义为「受到启发的」
由 inspiration 加 -al 构成，义为「鼓舞人心的」

senses.title: To give an urge or confidence
senses.definition: to give someone the wish, courage, or energy to do something important
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人做重要之事的愿望、勇气或力量
senses.example: The coach inspired the team to play beyond their level.
senses.exampleCN: 教练激励球队打出超常的水平。
senses.why: Latin spirare means to breathe; in- adds "in", so to inspire is literally to breathe courage into someone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 spirare 意为「呼吸」；in- 加「向内」，所以 inspire 字面上是「把勇气吹进某人」。

senses.title: To be the cause of an idea
senses.definition: to make someone have a new idea or create something, often without intending to
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生新想法或创作出作品，往往并非有意为之
senses.example: The old harbour inspired her best paintings.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老港口激发了她最好的画作。
senses.why: The breath enters from outside: a place or a person fills the mind with an idea.
senses.whyCN: 「气」从外面吹进来：一个地方或一个人让头脑里充满了想法。

senses.title: To cause a feeling
senses.definition: to produce a strong feeling such as trust, fear, or respect in other people
senses.definitionCN: 在他人心中产生信任、恐惧或尊敬等强烈情绪
senses.example: His calm voice inspired confidence in the passengers.
senses.exampleCN: 他沉稳的声音让乘客产生了信心。
senses.why: Feelings are breathed into people too, so the same verb covers courage, awe and confidence.
senses.whyCN: 情绪同样是被「吹进」人心的，所以同一动词也覆盖勇气、敬畏与信心。

intro.en: Inspire comes from Latin inspirare "to breathe in", a verb that became especially common in religious writing.
intro.cn: inspire 来自拉丁语 inspirare「吹气进去、呼吸」，这个动词在宗教文献中尤其常见。

items.en: Spirare "to breathe" is the root behind spirit, soul and breath words.
items.cn: spirare「呼吸」是 spirit、soul 等「气息」类词的词根。

items.en: Inspirare meant both to breathe in and to blow into something.
items.cn: inspirare 既指吸气，也指把气吹进某物。

items.en: In Christian Latin it described god breathing spirit into a person.
items.cn: 基督教拉丁语用它描述神把灵吹入人身。

items.en: Old French inspirer brought the verb into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 inspirer 把这一动词带入中古英语。

items.en: The modern sense of encouraging or stimulating an idea grows in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 现代「激励、启发」义在十七世纪发展起来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares Latin spir- "breathe"; the near-meaning group holds other verbs of encouragement.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 spir-「呼吸」；近义组收其他表示「鼓励」的动词。

entries.definition: The breath of life or a mood, from the same breathing root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「精神、情绪」，词根同为「呼吸」。

entries.definition: To breathe, with the prefix re- meaning back or again.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「呼吸」，前缀 re- 表「回、再」。

entries.definition: To come to an end, literally to breathe out for the last time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「到期、死亡」，字面是「呼出最后一口气」。

entries.definition: To give someone courage, plainer than inspire.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「鼓励」，比 inspire 朴素直白。

entries.definition: To give a reason for acting, often in a practical context.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激发动机」，多用于实际情境。

entries.definition: To rouse interest or activity, especially thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「刺激、激发」，多指激发兴趣或思考。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the breathing root spir- and the prepositions inspire takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「呼吸」词根 spir- 以及 inspire 所带的介词。

normal.en: spir- is breath: to inspire is to breathe in courage.
normal.cn: spir- 是呼吸：inspire 就是吸入勇气。

normal.en: Spirit, respire and expire all come from breathing.
normal.cn: spirit、respire、expire 都源于「呼吸」。

normal.en: Be inspired by someone, and inspire someone to act.
normal.cn: 受某人启发，也去激励别人行动。

normal.en: Leaders inspire confidence even when the news is bad.
normal.cn: 坏消息来了，领导者仍能激发信心。

normal.en: An inspiring talk changes what the audience does next week.
normal.cn: 鼓舞人心的演讲改变了听众下周的行动。

abstract.en: Picture a slow breath blown onto a dying ember.
abstract.cn: 想象一口慢气吹在将熄的炭火上。

abstract.en: Inspiration arrives from outside the mind, like air.
abstract.cn: 灵感像空气一样从头脑之外进来。

abstract.en: People remember who breathed courage into them.
abstract.cn: 人总记得是谁给自己吹入过勇气。

examples.en: Her calm manner inspired trust among the patients.
examples.cn: 她沉静的态度让病人产生了信任。

examples.en: The mountain village inspired several of his novels.
examples.cn: 那个山村激发了他好几部小说的灵感。

examples.en: The coach inspired the young players to keep trying.
examples.cn: 教练激励年轻球员继续努力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬死派」——鼓起勇气硬要派出去，就是被激励了

root: 拉丁语 spirare「呼吸、吹气」→ in- + spirare = inspirare「吸气；吹气进去」→ 基督教拉丁语指神把灵吹入人身 → 古法语 inspirer → 中古英语。spir- 也见于 spirit、respire、expire、conspire。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: breathing courage into people, filling minds with ideas, and raising a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：把勇气吹进人心、让头脑充满想法，以及激起某种情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a breath is blown onto a weak flame and it rises.
core.cn: 核心意象：一口气吹向微弱的火苗，火焰窜高。

branches.en: THE COACH: courage is given, and action follows.
branches.cn: 教练这条线：勇气被给予，行动随之而来。

branches.en: THE STUDIO: a place fills the mind with ideas.
branches.cn: 画室这条线：一个地方让头脑充满想法。

branches.en: THE HALL: a voice raises confidence or awe.
branches.cn: 大厅这条线：声音引起信心或敬畏。

branches.en: THE LINK: the feeling is always breathed in from someone else.
branches.cn: 连接线：情绪总是从别人那里被吹入。

branches.en: THE TONE: the idea sense is quieter and less active.
branches.cn: 语气线：「启发」义更安静、更不主动。

intro.en: Inspire is in- "into" plus the Latin breathing root spir-, with a French verb ending.
intro.cn: inspire 是 in-「向内」加拉丁「呼吸」词根 spir-，再带法语动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare, inspirare and the noun inspiratio are all recorded in classical and Christian texts.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spirare、inspirare 及名词 inspiratio 在古典与基督教文献中均有记载。

items.example: It marks the breath going in.
The root appears in spirit and expire.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根见于 spirit 与 expire。

items.example: The compound is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这一复合动词是直接来源。
Inspiration 指这种作用的结果。

items.example: Inspiring describes a person or event.
Re- adds the idea of return.

definition_en: a formal set of actions on an important occasion, or formal polite behaviour
core_image: 一群人按固定次序完成一整套动作
scene: 婚礼上宾客按顺序站好，等待交换誓言。 The wedding ceremony lasted an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 ceremony 指「典礼」（第 1 个义项：重要场合的正式仪式）；句意是婚礼仪式持续了一个小时。

senses.title: A formal event
senses.definition: a formal set of actions performed on an important public or religious occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在重要公共或宗教场合进行的一整套正式动作
senses.example: The graduation ceremony begins at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业典礼九点开始。
senses.why: The Latin source named a sacred rite, and the word still keeps that sense of a fixed set of actions.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源指宗教仪式，这个词仍保留整套固定动作的含义。

senses.title: Formal polite behaviour
senses.definition: the formal behaviour expected on polite occasions, sometimes seen as unnecessary
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌场合所要求的正式举止，有时被视为多余
senses.example: They greeted us without ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他们不拘礼节地跟我们打了招呼。
senses.why: Once a rite sets the proper forms of address, following those forms becomes a kind of ceremony in daily life.
senses.whyCN: 仪式一旦规定了得体的称呼方式，遵守这些形式在日常生活中也就成了一种客套。

intro.en: Ceremony comes from the Latin word for a sacred rite, and English first used it for religious observance.
intro.cn: ceremony 源自拉丁语中表示宗教仪式的词，英语最初用它指宗教礼拜。

items.en: Caerimonia named a religious rite and the awe that went with it.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caerimonia 指宗教仪式以及伴随的敬畏。

items.en: The adjective caeremonialis described what belonged to such rites.
items.cn: 形容词 caeremonialis 描述与这类仪式相关的事物。

items.en: Old French ceremonie carried the word into court and church usage.
items.cn: 古法语 ceremonie 把该词带入宫廷与教会用语。

items.en: English ceremony first means a religious observance or a formal rite.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语 ceremony 先指宗教礼拜或正式仪式。

items.en: The word widens to weddings, openings and the polite forms called ceremony.
items.cn: 词义扩展到婚礼、开幕式以及被称为客套的礼节。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the ceremony family, while the meaning group lists rites and formal occasions.
note.cn: 形近组沿 ceremony 词族展开，近义组列出仪式与正式场合的说法。

entries.definition: connected with formal ceremonies
very formal and correct in behaviour
in a very formal manner
a fixed religious act
a set of actions always done the same way
entries.definitionCN: 总按同样方式完成的一套动作

entries.definition: a formal religious gathering

normalIntro.en: These hooks link the fixed order of a rite to weddings, openings and polite distance.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把仪式的固定次序与婚礼、开幕式以及礼貌的距离联系起来。

normal.en: A ceremony is a set order of actions: everyone knows where to stand and what to say.
normal.cn: ceremony 是固定次序的动作：谁站哪里、说什么都有定规。

normal.en: Wedding ceremony and opening ceremony both mark a moment people want to remember.
normal.cn: wedding ceremony 与 opening ceremony 都标记人们想记住的时刻。

normal.en: Without ceremony means doing something plainly, with no polite fuss.
normal.cn: without ceremony 意为不带客套、直截了当地做事。

normal.en: To stand on ceremony is to insist on polite forms and distance.
normal.cn: stand on ceremony 就是坚持礼数与距离。

normal.en: Ceremonial is the adjective for the event, ceremonious for a stiff person.
normal.cn: ceremonial 形容仪式本身，ceremonious 形容拘谨的人。

abstract.en: Picture a line of people moving in step through a hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一队人踩着同一节拍穿过大厅。

abstract.en: Picture a stage with ribbons, speeches and a fixed order of turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一个有彩带、致辞和固定顺序的舞台。

abstract.en: Picture two people bowing slightly instead of shaking hands.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人微微鞠躬而不是握手。

examples.en: The award ceremony was held in the main hall.
examples.cn: 颁奖典礼在大厅举行。

examples.en: She left the room without ceremony.
examples.cn: 她不拘礼节地离开了房间。

examples.en: The old ceremony is performed every spring.
examples.cn: 这项古老的仪式每年春天举行。

dict_mnemonic.text: cere 联想到「因此」：因为重要，所以要按固定次序走完一整套动作，这就是仪式。

root: 源自拉丁语 caerimonia（宗教仪式、敬畏），经古法语 ceremonie 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The sacred rite gives the event sense, and the required forms of behaviour give the politeness sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 宗教仪式给出活动义，被要求的行为形式则给出礼节义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fixed sequence of actions performed in public.
core.cn: 核心意象：在众人面前按固定次序完成的一套动作。

branches.en: The event sense keeps the full public performance.
branches.cn: 活动义保留完整的公开仪式。

branches.en: The politeness sense shrinks the rite into manners.
branches.cn: 礼节义把仪式缩减为举止。

branches.en: Both rest on actions that follow a set order.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在按固定次序进行的动作上。

branches.en: Weddings, openings and graduations supply the modern occasions.
branches.cn: 婚礼、开幕式与毕业典礼提供现代场合。

branches.en: Phrases such as without ceremony reject the polite forms.
branches.cn: without ceremony 一类短语否定这些礼貌形式。

intro.en: Ceremony extends into ceremonial and ceremonious, two adjectives with different shades.
intro.cn: ceremony 扩展出 ceremonial 与 ceremonious 两个含义有别的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Caerimonia and caeremonialis are the Latin noun and adjective behind the English family.
latinIntro.cn: caerimonia 与 caeremonialis 是英语词族背后的拉丁语名词与形容词。

items.exampleCN: 她那郑重的鞠躬显得冷淡。

items.example: A judge officiated at the wedding.

latinEntries.exampleCN: caerimonia 以 ceremonie 进入法语。

definition_zh: 使普及；使流行；使通俗易懂；推广
definition_en: to make something widely known, used or liked, especially by presenting it in a form ordinary people can understand
core_image: 一位老师把厚书上的公式拆成几张手绘图，贴在菜市场门口的黑板上
scene: 社区活动室里，退休工程师把复杂的电路画成几笔简图，围坐的老人边听边点头。 His talks helped popularize basic electronics among people who had never opened a machine.
sceneCN: 这里 popularize 指「使通俗易懂并广为流传」（第 2 个义项：把专门内容讲到普通人也能懂）；句意为他的讲座让从没拆过机器的人也能听懂基础电子知识。图中可辨识场景：活动室里的简图、围坐的老人、点头的动作。

pos.zh: 使普及；使流行；使通俗易懂；推广

derivatives.zh: 由 popularize 加 -ation 构成，义为「普及；通俗化」
由 popularize 加 -er 构成，义为「普及者；推广者」
由 popularize 去掉动词后缀 -ize 得到，义为「大众的；受欢迎的」
由 popular 加 -ity 构成，义为「受欢迎；人气」

senses.title: To make something widely known and used
senses.definition: to cause an idea, product or practice to become known and used by a large number of ordinary people
senses.definitionCN: 使观念、产品或做法被大量普通人知道并使用
senses.example: Cheap printing helped popularize the novel in the nineteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价印刷在十九世纪推动了小说的普及。
senses.why: Popularize is popular plus -ize, a suffix meaning to make something have a quality; to popularize is therefore to make a thing belong to the people.
senses.whyCN: popularize 是 popular 加 -ize，这个后缀表示使某物具有某种性质；所以「使普及」就是让某样东西归到民众手里。

senses.title: To present specialist material in plain terms
senses.definition: to explain a technical or academic subject in language that non-specialists can follow
senses.definitionCN: 用非专业者也能跟上的语言解释技术或学术内容
senses.example: The series popularized astronomy without watering down the science.
senses.exampleCN: 这套节目普及了天文知识，却没有把科学内容兑水。
senses.why: If a subject is to belong to everybody, its language has to leave the laboratory, so the verb also names the work of turning jargon into plain speech.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问要属于所有人，它的语言就得走出实验室，于是这个动词也用来指把术语翻成大白话的那份工作。

senses.title: To promote something to the public
senses.definition: to market or promote a product, place or idea so that ordinary people accept it
senses.definitionCN: 为产品、地点或观念做营销宣传，使普通人接受
senses.example: The campaign popularized a drink that few people had heard of.
senses.exampleCN: 这场推广让一种很少有人听过的饮料流行起来。
senses.why: Once the verb means making a thing common, businesses borrow it for the deliberate work of pushing a product into ordinary hands.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个动词指让东西变普遍，商家就借它来指有意识地把产品推到大众人手里的工作。

intro.en: Popularize was not inherited from Latin: English built it from the adjective popular and the suffix -ize, and Latin has no verb popularizare.
intro.cn: popularize 不是从拉丁语继承来的：英语用形容词 popular 加后缀 -ize 造出它，拉丁语里并没有 popularizare 这个动词。

items.en: Populus, the people as a body, is the root behind the whole family.
items.cn: populus 指作为整体的民众，是整族词背后的根。

items.en: Popularis, of the people, supplied the stem that English later took as popular.
items.cn: popularis 意为属于民众的，提供词干，英语后来把它取作 popular。

items.en: English borrowed popular through French and used it for what is common, public or widely liked.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入 popular，用它指公共的、大众的或广受喜爱的。

items.en: The verb ending -izein, taken into Latin as -izare and into English as -ize, means to make, do or act in a certain way.
items.cn: 动词词尾 -izein 经拉丁语 -izare 进入英语作 -ize，意为使成为、做、按某种方式行事。

items.en: English joined the two around the early nineteenth century, when cheap print and public lectures were carrying science to ordinary readers.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪初前后把两者拼在一起，那正是廉价印刷与公开讲座把科学带给普通读者的年代。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same word family, all resting on populus; the near-meaning group holds other verbs for spreading and simplifying.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个词族，都依托 populus；近义组收表示传播与简化的其他动词。

entries.definition: Liked by many people; of the people.
entries.definitionCN: 受许多人喜爱的；大众的。

entries.definition: The state of being liked by many people.
The act or result of making something widely known.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物广为人知的行为或结果；普及。

entries.definition: A person who makes a subject or product widely known.
entries.definitionCN: 把学科或产品带给大众的人。

entries.definition: To cause something to reach more people or places.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物传到更多人或地方。

entries.definition: To help something grow, sell or become accepted.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助某物增长、销售或被接受；推广。

entries.definition: To make something easier to understand or do.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物更容易理解或做到。

normalIntro.en: The word is an English construction on a Latin stem, and its senses follow one line: bring something down to the level of the people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是英语在拉丁词干上造出来的，几个义项沿着一条线走：把东西带到普通人够得着的高度。

normal.en: Popularize is popular plus -ize; the suffix says make, so the verb says make it belong to the people.
normal.cn: popularize 是 popular 加 -ize；后缀表示「使」，动词的意思就是让它归到民众手里。

normal.en: There was no Latin verb popularizare; the word was built inside English from an adjective and a suffix.
normal.cn: 拉丁语里没有 popularizare 这个动词；这个词是英语用形容词加后缀造的。

normal.en: Science, theories and products are its usual objects, because all three need translating for a crowd.
normal.cn: 科学、理论和产品是它常见的对象，因为这三样都需要为大众翻译一遍。

normal.en: Popularization is the noun, popularizer the person who does it.
normal.cn: popularization 是名词，popularizer 是做这件事的人。

normal.en: The word follows the -ize pattern of modernize and globalize: make something spread.
normal.cn: 这个词沿用 modernize 与 globalize 的 -ize 模式：使某样东西扩散。

abstract.en: To popularize is to carry something heavy down the stairs to where people are standing.
abstract.cn: 普及就是把某样沉重的东西搬下楼梯，搬到人们站着的地方。

abstract.en: A diagram that replaces a page of equations has done the work the word names.
abstract.cn: 一张图替掉一页公式，就已经完成了这个词所指的那件事。

abstract.en: Making a thing common and making it liked are the same motion seen from two ends.
abstract.cn: 让东西变普遍，与让东西被喜欢，是同一个动作的两端。

examples.en: Television did more than any book to popularize the sport.
examples.cn: 电视对这项运动普及的推动超过了任何一本书。

examples.en: She popularized the method by teaching it in short videos.
examples.cn: 她用短视频讲这个方法，使它流行起来。

examples.en: The museum works to popularize local history among children.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆致力于在孩子们中间普及本地历史。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泡普乐来兹」——把东西泡进普通人的快乐里，让它变得人人都会，就是 popularize：推广普及。

root: popular（大众的，源自拉丁语 populus 民众）+ 后缀 -ize（使……化）；拉丁语并无 popularizare 这一动词，popularize 是英语后造的词。

sensesIntro.en: One motion runs through the senses: take something out of the hands of specialists and put it into the hands of ordinary people.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项贯穿着同一个动作：把东西从专家手里拿出来，放到普通人手里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a teacher turning a page of formulas into a few hand-drawn arrows, pinned up where everyone walks past.
core.cn: 核心意象：老师把一页公式画成几个手绘箭头，贴在人人经过的地方。

branches.en: a cheap edition that puts a novel in every pocket
branches.cn: 让小说进到每个人口袋的廉价版本

branches.en: a diagram that turns a formula into three arrows
branches.cn: 把公式变成三个箭头的示意图

branches.en: a poster that makes a new drink look familiar
branches.cn: 让新饮料看着眼熟的海报

branches.en: a lecture that is both simple and passed on
branches.cn: 既讲得简单又被口口相传的讲座

branches.en: a plain explanation that ends up as an advertisement
branches.cn: 一段通俗讲解最终变成广告

intro.en: A Latin stem for the people meets an English suffix of making. The family divides cleanly: -ar makes the adjective, -ity the noun of state, -ize this verb of making, and -ation or -er the act and the person.
intro.cn: 表示民众的拉丁词干遇上表示「使」的英语后缀。整族词分工清楚：-ar 造形容词，-ity 造表状态的名词，-ize 造这个表「使……」的动词，-ation 与 -er 再分别指行为和做这件事的人。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: the act of making something common
a person who makes something common

definition_zh: 乐意；意愿；愿意帮忙的态度
definition_en: the quality of being ready and glad to do something when it is needed
core_image: 会场里主持人问谁愿意先上，一排手几乎是同时举了起来
scene: 老师刚问有没有人愿意主持班会，角落里那只手就举得很高。 Her willingness to take the difficult task surprised everyone in the office.
sceneCN: 这里 willingness 是「乐意、意愿」（第 1 个义项：随时愿意去做的那种态度）；句意为她愿意接下难办的活，让办公室所有人都吃了一惊。会场里一排手几乎同时举起，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A ready attitude
senses.definition: the state of being ready to do something when asked or needed
senses.definitionCN: 被请求或需要时随时愿意去做的状态
senses.example: Her willingness to take the difficult task surprised everyone in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 她愿意接下难办的活，让办公室所有人都吃了一惊。
senses.why: The ending -ness turns the adjective willing into the trait itself, something you can show or lack.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ness 把形容词 willing 变成这种特质本身，一种你可以表现出来也可以缺少的东西。

senses.title: Eagerness to help others
senses.definition: a friendly readiness that shows itself in small acts of service
senses.definitionCN: 一种友善的愿意，表现在一件件小小的帮助里
senses.example: The neighbours remembered his willingness more than the money he gave.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们记得更多的是他的乐于帮忙，而不是他出的钱。
senses.why: When the readiness looks outward it becomes a social virtue rather than a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 当这份愿意朝向别人，它就成了一种社会美德，而不只是私人的情绪。

senses.title: In business and surveys
senses.definition: the amount of effort or money people say they are ready to give, as in market research
senses.definitionCN: 在市场调查中指人们自称愿意付出的努力或金钱
senses.example: The survey measured customers' willingness to pay for faster delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查测量了顾客为更快的送达付费的意愿。
senses.why: Researchers took the everyday trait and gave it a number, turning a feeling into data.
senses.whyCN: 研究者把这日常特质变成一个数字，把一种感受变成了数据。

intro.en: Willingness is the noun of state built on willing, which grows from will; Old English willan meant to wish.
intro.cn: willingness 是由 willing 构成的状态名词，willing 出自 will；古英语 willan 意为希望、愿意。

items.en: willa was the mind that wishes, and lystan named the desire itself.
items.cn: willa 指愿想的心，lystan 指那份欲望本身。

items.en: The verb willan was a core verb of choosing, used of God, kings and ordinary people.
items.cn: 动词 willan 是选择的核心动词，用于神、君王和普通人。

items.en: willing, ready in mind, gained the noun ending -nesse to name the quality.
items.cn: 愿意的 willing 获得名词词尾 -nesse，用来命名这种品质。

items.en: The spelling settled on -ness and the word spread into law, religion and trade.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 -ness，这个词扩展到法律、宗教和贸易。

items.en: In the last century it became a measured variable in surveys of how much people will pay.
items.cn: 上个世纪它成了调查中可测量的变量，用来衡量人们愿意付多少。

note.en: The first group collects the same family, the second other nouns for an inner drive.
note.cn: 第一组收同一个词族，第二组收其他表示内在驱动的名词。

entries.definition: Ready to help, the adjective behind it.
Doing something with a glad heart.
Reluctance, the lack of this trait.
Stubborn following of one's own wish.
Being prepared and quick to act.
Strong keen desire to begin.
The reason that pushes someone to act.

normalIntro.en: Willingness is the state noun, so its ending -ness works like the -ness in kindness and readiness.
normalIntro.cn: willingness 是状态名词，词尾 -ness 与 kindness、readiness 里的 -ness 一样。

normal.en: Three steps: will, willing, willingness. Each step makes it more abstract.
normal.cn: 三步：will、willing、willingness，每一步都更抽象一点。

normal.en: The -ness ending means the quality itself, as in kindness and darkness.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ness 表示品质本身，如 kindness、darkness。

normal.en: Unwillingness simply pulls the whole word to the opposite side.
normal.cn: unwillingness 只是把整个词拉到相反的一边。

normal.en: Willingness is invisible, so it must be shown by a hand or a step.
normal.cn: 意愿是无形的，所以必须用一只手或一步路来证明。

normal.en: Remember the contrast with ability: ability is what you can do, willingness is what you will do.
normal.cn: 记住与 ability 的对照：ability 是你能做什么，willingness 是你愿意做什么。

abstract.en: A row of hands rising at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 一排手在同一瞬间举起。

abstract.en: Warmth in the voice that says yes.
abstract.cn: 说「好」时声音里的温度。

abstract.en: A door unlocked before anyone knocks.
abstract.cn: 还没人敲门，门就已经开了锁。

examples.en: Her willingness to listen made him talk for an hour.
examples.cn: 她愿意倾听，让他讲了整整一个小时。

examples.en: The company praised the staff for their willingness to work extra hours.
examples.cn: 公司赞扬员工愿意加班。

examples.en: Without your willingness, none of this could have started.
examples.cn: 没有你的愿意，这一切都无从开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: willing（愿意的）+ ness（状态）—— 愿意这种状态，就是「乐意、意愿」。

root: 古英语 willan（希望）→ will → willing（形容词）→ willingness；同族有 willingly、unwillingness。

sensesIntro.en: A private readiness first becomes a visible friendliness, then a number that surveys can measure.
sensesIntro.cn: 私下的愿意先变成看得见的友善，再变成一个调查能测量的数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifted high before the question has quite ended.
core.cn: 核心意象：问题还没完全说完，手已经高高举起。

branches.en: The trait branch: a person ready when the need appears.
branches.cn: 特质分支：需要一出现就准备好的人。

branches.en: The friendly branch: remembered for helping, not for money.
branches.cn: 友善分支：被记住的是帮忙，不是钱。

branches.en: The data branch: willingness to pay, written as a figure.
branches.cn: 数据分支：支付意愿被写成一个数字。

branches.en: The visible branch: what cannot be seen must be shown by acts.
branches.cn: 可见分支：看不见的东西得用行动表现出来。

branches.en: The abstract branch: a feeling turned into a quality and then a measure.
branches.cn: 抽象分支：感受先变成品质，再变成度量。

intro.en: Willingness stacks the native root will with the adjective -ing and the noun -ness; un- flips it to the opposite.
intro.cn: willingness 把本土词根 will、形容词词尾 -ing 与名词词尾 -ness 叠在一起；un- 把它翻成反面。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, so the Latin column lists only borrowed ideas that shade its meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属于日耳曼语，所以拉丁栏只列出给它的意义作注的借入词。

items.example: It is the base of the whole family.
The same root turns to anger.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词根转向了愤怒。

items.meaning: the power to choose by oneself
items.example: The philosophical centre of the stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在哲学上的中心。

definition_en: to surprise someone very much, or to shock by something hard to believe
core_image: 一声雷在头顶炸开，人愣在原地
scene: 魔术师从帽子里变出一只活鸽子。 The trick astonished the children.
sceneCN: 这里 astonish 是「使惊讶」（第 1 个义项：因意外而让人愣住）；句意是这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。

pos.zh: 动词：使大为惊讶；使震惊

senses.title: Surprise greatly
senses.definition: to surprise someone very much by something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 因出乎意料之事而让人极为惊讶
senses.example: The trick astonished the children.
senses.exampleCN: 这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。
senses.why: Astonish goes back to Latin extonare, 'to strike with thunder', so the original picture is a person stunned by a clap overhead.
senses.whyCN: astonish 可追溯到拉丁语 extonare「雷击」，最初的画面就是人被头顶的一声雷震得愣住。

senses.title: Shock by something hard to believe
senses.definition: to shock someone with news or an event that seems unbelievable
senses.definitionCN: 用难以相信的消息或事件使人震惊
senses.example: The scale of the damage astonished the inspectors.
senses.exampleCN: 损失的规模让检查人员震惊。
senses.why: When the thunderbolt is bad news rather than a trick, the same stunned stillness reads as shock, which is why the word also covers disbelief at something grave.
senses.whyCN: 当那道雷不是戏法而是坏消息时，同样的僵住就成了一种震惊，所以这个词也能表示对严重事件的难以置信。

intro.en: Astonish is a thunder word: its ancestors describe being struck by lightning.
intro.cn: astonish 是个打雷的词，它的祖辈词描述被雷电击中。

items.en: tonare meant 'to thunder'.
items.cn: tonare 意为「打雷」。

items.en: extonare meant 'to strike with thunder'.
items.cn: extonare 意为「以雷击打」。

items.en: estoner meant 'to stun or amaze'.
items.cn: estoner 意为「震住、使惊愕」。

items.en: astonen meant 'to stun the mind'.
items.cn: astonen 意为「使心神震住」。

items.en: The spelling settled as astonish, with the thunder forgotten.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 astonish，打雷的画面渐渐被遗忘。

note.en: The look-alike group is the astonish family; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of surprise.
note.cn: 形近组是 astonish 词族；近义组是其他表示惊讶的动词。

entries.definition: great surprise
extremely surprising
to shock with surprise
to fill with wonder
to cause unexpected wonder
to upset with a sudden event

normalIntro.en: Think of a thunderclap that leaves a person standing still.
normalIntro.cn: 想象一声雷把人劈在原地不动。

normal.en: The subject is the startling thing, the object is the person.
normal.cn: 主语是令人吃惊的事物，宾语是人。

normal.en: The adjective astonishing describes the thing, astonished the person.
normal.cn: astonishing 形容事物，astonished 形容人。

normal.en: The noun is astonishment.
normal.cn: 名词是 astonishment。

normal.en: It is stronger than surprise.
normal.cn: 它比 surprise 程度更重。

normal.en: The middle syllable is stressed: as-TON-ish.
normal.cn: 重音在中间音节。

abstract.en: See a dove pulled from an empty hat.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸽子从空帽子里被拎出来。

abstract.en: See a listener frozen with a cup halfway to the mouth.
abstract.cn: 想象听的人僵住，杯子停在半空。

abstract.en: See a flash and then a room gone silent.
abstract.cn: 想象一道闪光之后，整个房间静下来。

examples.en: The trick astonished the children.
examples.cn: 这个戏法让孩子们大为惊讶。

examples.en: The scale of the damage astonished the inspectors.
examples.cn: 损失的规模让检查人员震惊。

examples.en: She astonished us all by finishing first.
examples.cn: 她第一个完成，让我们都很吃惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词源里藏着「雷」：拉丁语 extonare 是被雷击中。人被雷劈中般僵住，就是大为惊讶；遇到难以相信的坏消息，就是震惊。

root: 源自拉丁语 extonare「以雷击打」，由 ex- 加强语气与 tonare「打雷」构成，经古法语 estoner 进入英语；由「被雷震住」引申为大为惊讶与震惊。

sensesIntro.en: A wonderful trick and a terrible scale of damage can both freeze a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 精彩的戏法与骇人的损失规模，都能让人僵在原地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thunderclap directly overhead.
core.cn: 核心意象：头顶炸开的一声雷。

branches.en: astonish the children
branches.cn: 让孩子们大为惊讶

branches.en: an astonishing result
branches.cn: 惊人的结果

branches.en: be astonished at the news
branches.cn: 听到消息很惊讶

branches.en: the damage astonished the inspectors
branches.cn: 损失让检查人员震惊

branches.en: to my astonishment
branches.cn: 令我震惊的是

intro.en: The word carries a hidden thunder root, ton, visible also in detonate.
intro.cn: 这个词藏着表示「雷」的词根 ton，在 detonate 里也能看到。

latinIntro.en: Latin tonare, 'to thunder', and its compounds entered English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tonare「打雷」及其复合词经法语进入英语。

definition_en: a long gun fired from the shoulder, or to search through something quickly
core_image: 士兵倚在墙边擦拭步枪
scene: 士兵把步枪靠在墙边，仔细擦拭长长的枪管。 The soldier leaned the rifle against the wall and cleaned the barrel.
sceneCN: 这里 rifle 是「步枪」（第 1 个义项：可从肩上射击的长枪）；句意：士兵把步枪靠在墙边，仔细擦拭长长的枪管。

senses.title: A long gun
senses.definition: a long gun held against the shoulder
senses.definitionCN: 抵在肩上射击的长枪
senses.example: The guard carried an old rifle.
senses.exampleCN: 卫兵拿着一支旧步枪。
senses.why: The grooved barrel is the heart of a rifle.
senses.whyCN: 带膛线的枪管是步枪的核心。

senses.title: Searching quickly
senses.definition: to search through something in a hurry
senses.definitionCN: 匆忙地翻找某处
senses.example: She rifled through the drawer for her keys.
senses.exampleCN: 她在抽屉里匆忙翻找钥匙。
senses.why: Hurried hands scrape through things like a groove.
senses.whyCN: 匆忙的手像划过沟槽一样翻动东西。

senses.title: Stealing from a place
senses.definition: to search a place and take what is inside
senses.definitionCN: 翻遍某处并拿走里面的东西
senses.example: Thieves had rifled the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 小偷洗劫了那栋空房子。
senses.why: A quick search can turn into plunder.
senses.whyCN: 快速翻找可能变成掠夺。

intro.en: The gun sense comes from a grooved barrel; the verb comes from Old French rifler, to scratch or plunder.

core_image: 搅拌机里旋成漩涡的果泥
scene: 搅拌机转起来，果块渐渐化成漩涡。 Blend the fruit with a little milk.

混合，把不同成分调和在一起的过程

senses.title: To mix smoothly together
senses.definition: to mix two or more things until they are combined
senses.definitionCN: 把两种或更多东西搅到合为一体
senses.example: Blend the fruit with a little milk.
senses.exampleCN: 把水果加一点牛奶搅匀。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from an old verb meaning to mix.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，来自一个意为混合的古动词。

senses.title: To fit in with surroundings
senses.definition: to look or sound natural together
senses.definitionCN: 放在一起看起来或听起来自然
senses.example: The new houses blend with the old street.
senses.exampleCN: 新房子与老街很协调。
senses.why: Things that mix well also look as if they belong together.
senses.whyCN: 混得好的东西，看起来也像是本来就在一起。

senses.title: A mixture of things
senses.definition: a combination of different things
senses.definitionCN: 不同东西组合成的整体
senses.example: This tea is a blend of three leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 这款茶由三种茶叶拼配而成。
senses.why: The verb became a noun for the result of mixing.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为名词，指混合的结果。

intro.en: Blend came from an Old English verb for mixing, reinforced by Norse.
intro.cn: blend 来自古英语表示混合的动词，并受到诺斯语影响。

items.en: blandan meant to mix.
items.cn: blandan 意为混合。

items.en: blend named a mixture of teas or wines.
items.cn: blend 指茶或酒的拼配。

items.cn: 如今 blend 兼指混合、协调与混合物。

normal.en: Blend in means fit with the people around.
normal.cn: blend in 表示融入周围。

normal.en: A tea blend combines several leaves.
normal.cn: a tea blend 把几种茶叶拼在一起。

normal.en: A blender is the machine that does it.
normal.cn: blender 是做这件事的机器。

normal.en: Blend is both verb and noun.

definition_en: annoyed by waiting, or wanting something to happen very soon
core_image: 排队时不停看表、把重心从一只脚换到另一只脚的人
scene: 银行只开了一个窗口，队尾那位每隔十秒就看一眼手机。 He grew impatient before the clerk had even called the first number.
sceneCN: 这里 impatient 是「不耐烦的」（第 1 个义项：因等待而恼火），句意是柜员还没叫第一个号，他就已经不耐烦了。画面里有只开一个窗口的银行和不停看表的人。

pos.zh: 形容词：不耐烦的、急躁的；急切的

senses.title: Annoyed by delay
senses.definition: irritated because something takes longer than you want
senses.definitionCN: 因某事耗时过久而感到恼火
senses.example: The driver became impatient at the third red light.
senses.exampleCN: 第三个红灯时司机已经不耐烦了。
senses.why: Patient here means enduring, and the negative prefix says the endurance has run out.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 patient 意为「能忍受的」，否定前缀说明忍耐已经耗尽。

senses.title: Eager for something to happen
senses.definition: very keen and unable to wait calmly for a result
senses.definitionCN: 非常渴望结果而无法平静等待
senses.example: She was impatient for the exam results.
senses.exampleCN: 她急切地等着考试成绩。
senses.why: Losing the will to wait can point forward as well as backward, so the word also names hopeful eagerness.
senses.whyCN: 失去等待的耐性既可指向过去也可指向未来，于是这个词也指带着期待的急切。

senses.title: Short and sharp in manner
senses.definition: describing a movement or tone that shows irritation
senses.definitionCN: 形容流露出恼意的手势或语气
senses.example: He answered with an impatient wave of the hand.
senses.exampleCN: 他不耐烦地摆了摆手作答。
senses.why: Inward irritation soon shows as outward gesture, and English lets the adjective describe the gesture itself.
senses.whyCN: 内心的恼火很快外化为手势，英语允许这个形容词直接描述手势。

intro.en: Impatient negates the Latin word for suffering, for patience was the ability to bear things.
intro.cn: impatient 是对拉丁语「忍受」一词的否定，因为 patience 本指承受之力。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer or to undergo, and patiens described one who endured.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pati 意为忍受、经受，patiens 形容能够承受的人。

items.en: Impatiens added the negative: unable to bear, easily provoked by waiting.
items.cn: 加否定前缀成 impatiens：无法承受，容易被等待激怒。

items.en: The plant we call impatient got the name for bursting its seed pods at a touch.
items.cn: 我们称作凤仙花的那种植物，因蒴果一碰就炸而得名。

items.en: French used impacient, and the form passed into English writing.
items.cn: 法语作 impacient，这一形式进入英语书写。

items.en: English fixed the spelling as impatient and kept both the waiting sense and the eager sense.
items.cn: 英语把拼写定为 impatient，兼收「等不下去」与「急切盼望」两种用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the patient family; the near-meaning group gathers words for irritation and hurry.
note.cn: 形近组收 patient 词族；近义组收表示烦躁与急促的词。

entries.definition: The state of being impatient.
In an impatient manner.
Able to wait calmly, the positive base word.
entries.definitionCN: 能够平静等待的，肯定形式。

entries.definition: Unable to stay still, often from boredom.
Mildly angry, without the specific cause of waiting.
Very keen to act; only the positive side of sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 非常想行动，只取第二个义项中积极的一面。

normalIntro.en: The hooks turn on the negative prefix and the hidden word for suffering inside patient.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子全靠否定前缀以及 patient 里藏着的「忍受」之意。

normal.en: Im- is not: impatient is not patient, and patient is the one who can suffer and wait.
normal.cn: im- 是不：impatient 就是不 patient，而 patient 本指能忍受、能等待的人。

normal.en: Im-patient, one m only: the prefix folds into the p that follows.
normal.cn: im-patient，只有一个 m：前缀并进了后面的 p。

normal.en: Three beats, stress the middle: im-PA-tient.
normal.cn: 三个拍子，重音在中间：im-PA-tient。

normal.en: The ending sounds like shent, the same soft sh that patient also carries.
normal.cn: 词尾读作 shent，与 patient 所带的那个柔和的 sh 相同。

normal.en: Impatient with people, impatient for news: two prepositions, two feelings.
normal.cn: impatient with 人，impatient for 消息：两个介词，两种心情。

abstract.en: The word quietly remembers that patience is a form of suffering bravely borne.
abstract.cn: 这个词悄悄记着：耐心原是一种被勇敢承受的痛苦。

abstract.en: Losing patience is losing the ability to let time pass, and clocks then seem to slow on purpose.
abstract.cn: 失去耐心就是失去让时间流过的能力，此后钟表仿佛故意变慢。

abstract.en: The same word covers impatience at a queue and eagerness for good news, since both refuse delay.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指排队时的烦躁，也指急盼好消息，因为两者都拒绝等待。

examples.en: Don't be so impatient; the train will come.
examples.cn: 别这么急躁，火车会来的。

examples.en: She was impatient to see her son again.
examples.cn: 她急切地想再见到儿子。

examples.en: The teacher was growing impatient with the same excuses.
examples.cn: 老师听到同样的借口渐渐不耐烦了。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 不 + patient 能忍耐的——不能忍，即不耐烦的

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: irritated by waiting, eager for what is coming, and showing that irritation in manner.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：因等待而恼、急切盼望将来的事，以及在举止上流露恼意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person shifting weight from foot to foot in a slow queue.
core.cn: 核心意象：慢队里不断换脚站着的人。

branches.cn: 排队线：红灯与慢窗口招来它。

branches.en: THE WAITING LINE: impatient for results is hopeful, not angry.
branches.cn: 等待线：急盼结果时是期盼而非恼怒。

branches.en: THE GESTURE LINE: a wave of the hand completes the meaning.
branches.cn: 手势线：一摆手就把意思说完了。

branches.en: THE TIME LINE: the root cause is always delay.
branches.cn: 时间线：根本原因始终是拖延。

definition_en: to look at something closely in order to judge its quality or find problems
core_image: 一双眼凑近齿轮，把每一道纹路都看一遍
scene: 车间里，质检员拿着记录板在机器之间慢慢走动。 An engineer came to inspect the bridge after the flood.
sceneCN: 这里 inspect 是「检查、视察」（第 1 个义项：仔细查看以判断质量或发现问题）；句意为洪水过后有工程师来检查这座桥。图中可辨识物件：记录板、齿轮、手电筒。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「检查；视察」

senses.title: To look at closely
senses.definition: to look at something carefully in order to judge it or find faults
senses.definitionCN: 为判断好坏或发现问题而仔细查看
senses.example: He inspected the tyres before the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途出发前他检查了轮胎。
senses.why: Inspectare is to look over and over: the eye goes into the detail on purpose.
senses.whyCN: inspectare 是「反复查看」：眼睛有目的地深入细节。

senses.title: To visit officially to check
senses.definition: to visit a place officially and check that rules or standards are being kept
senses.definitionCN: 以官方身份到某地查看规章或标准是否被遵守
senses.example: Officials will inspect the school next month.
senses.exampleCN: 官员们下个月将来视察这所学校。
senses.why: When the state does the looking, inspection becomes a formal visit with authority behind it.
senses.whyCN: 当由国家来看时，inspection 就成了有权威支撑的正式到访。

intro.en: Inspect is Latin in- plus specere "to look": to look into something on purpose.
intro.cn: inspect 是拉丁语 in- 加 specere「看」：有目的地往里面看。

items.en: Specere meant "to look, observe", the root of spectacle, species and respect.
items.cn: specere 意为「看、观察」，是 spectacle、species、respect 的词根。

items.en: Inspectare, a frequentative of inspicere, meant "to look into, examine repeatedly".
items.cn: inspectare 是 inspicere 的反复形式，意为「往里看、反复查看」。

items.en: The noun inspectio was used of examining property and accounts.
items.cn: 名词 inspectio 用于察看财产与账目。

items.en: English adopted inspect in the seventeenth century for official and technical checks.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪采用 inspect，用于官方与技术的检查。

items.en: Modern use spans tyres, factories, bridges, and imported goods.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖轮胎、工厂、桥梁与进口货物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of looking; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of checking.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「看」动词；近义组收其他表示查看的动词。

entries.definition: To look back at someone with esteem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「尊敬」，同根。

entries.definition: A person who watches an event.
To look up at someone with doubt.
To look at something in detail, often to test it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「检查、考查」，强调细究或测试。

entries.definition: To make sure something is correct or safe, quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「核对」，通常较快。

entries.definition: To look over a whole area or situation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「勘察、调查」，强调整体俯瞰。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use specere, the verb of looking, and the collocations the word takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用「看」的动词 specere，以及这个词的搭配。

normal.en: Specere is to look: to inspect is to look into something on purpose.
normal.cn: specere 是「看」：inspect 就是有目的地往里看。

normal.en: Respect, suspect and inspect are all ways of looking at someone.
normal.cn: respect、suspect、inspect 都是「看」的不同方式。

normal.en: An inspector inspects; an inspection is what he carries out.
normal.cn: inspector 负责 inspect，而 inspection 是他所做的检查。

normal.en: Inspect for damage means looking specifically for faults.
normal.cn: inspect for damage 意为专门查找破损。

normal.en: Goods are inspected before they leave the port.
normal.cn: 货物在离港前要接受查验。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass over a seam: the eye decides what the hand will fix.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜对准一道接缝：眼睛决定手该修哪里。

abstract.en: Inspection is trust replaced by evidence.
abstract.cn: 检查是用证据取代信任。

abstract.en: To inspect is to look with a question already in mind.
abstract.cn: 审视是带着问题去看。

examples.en: The car was inspected before it was sold.
examples.cn: 这辆车售出前接受过检查。

examples.en: Health officers inspect restaurants twice a year.
examples.cn: 卫生官员每年检查餐馆两次。

examples.en: She inspected the letter closely, looking for a date.
examples.cn: 她仔细查看那封信，想找日期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯派克特」——因要细细「看」，才去检查

root: 拉丁语 specere「看」加 in-「向内」构成 inspicere「往里看」，反复形式 inspectare 与名词 inspectio 经英语借入作 inspect；同根词有 respect、suspect、spectator、spectacle。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: looking closely at a thing, and looking over a place in an official role.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：仔细查看某物，以及以官方身份巡查某地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye brought close to a gear, following every groove.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛凑近齿轮，顺着每道沟纹看过去。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: goods are inspected before they are passed.
branches.cn: 车间这条线：货物在通过之前要受检。

branches.en: THE ROAD: tyres and brakes are inspected for safety.
branches.cn: 道路这条线：轮胎与刹车要检查是否安全。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: an official visit checks that standards are kept.
branches.cn: 学校这条线：官方到访核查标准是否被维持。

branches.en: THE PORT: customs officers inspect imported goods.
branches.cn: 港口这条线：海关人员查验进口货物。

branches.en: THE THREAD: both senses look with a judgement in mind, not for pleasure.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两种看都带着判断目的，而非为了欣赏。

intro.en: Inspect is a Latin prefix on the verb for looking, with a frequentative Latin stem.
intro.cn: inspect 是拉丁语前缀加「看」的动词，词干取反复形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere, inspicere, inspectare and inspectio are recorded, along with the related spectrum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere、inspicere、inspectare、inspectio 均有记录，还有相关的 spectrum。

items.example: It gives direction to the looking.

items.exampleCN: 它出现在 inspector 与 respect 中。

definition_en: covered with blood
core_image: 摔倒后擦破的膝盖
scene: 孩子摔倒，膝盖上渗出血迹。 He wiped his bloody knee with a tissue.
sceneCN: 这里 bloody 是「流血的」（第 1 个义项：沾着血的）；句意是他用纸巾擦掉膝盖上的血。

pos.zh: 形容词：流血的；血淋淋的
形容词：该死的，英式口语中加强语气

senses.title: Covered with blood
senses.definition: with blood on the surface
senses.definitionCN: 表面沾着血的
senses.example: He wiped his bloody knee with a tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 他用纸巾擦掉膝盖上的血。
senses.why: This is the literal sense, blood plus the adjective ending.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面义，由 blood 加形容词词尾构成。

senses.title: Involving much killing
senses.definition: with a lot of violence and death
senses.definitionCN: 伴随大量暴力与死亡的
senses.example: It was a long and bloody war.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一场漫长而血腥的战争。
senses.why: A scene full of blood became a description of violent conflict.
senses.whyCN: 满是血的场面，被用来形容暴力的冲突。

senses.title: Used as a strong British intensifier
senses.definition: used in British speech to add strong force
senses.definitionCN: 在英式口语中用来加强语气
senses.example: That was a bloody good meal.
senses.exampleCN: 那顿饭真是好极了。
senses.why: A word for blood became a mild swear word that adds force.
senses.whyCN: 表示血的词变成了加强语气的轻度粗话。

intro.en: Bloody is the plain adjective from blood, later used as a swear word.
intro.cn: bloody 是由 blood 加词尾构成的普通形容词，后来被用作粗话。

items.cn: 如今 bloody 既有字面义，也作语气加强词。

note.cn: 形近组共用 blood- 词干；近义组是血污与暴力类词。

normalIntro.cn: bloody 从描述血的事实出发，最后变成一种粗话。

normal.en: A bloody nose is a common literal use.
normal.cn: a bloody nose 是常见的字面用法。

normal.en: A bloody war means a war with much death.
